bull.b: The proposed Range combination could materially expand EQT’s production base, acreage inventory and midstream footprint. Greater scale may support lower breakeven costs, operating efficiencies and stronger bargaining power, reinforcing EQT’s competitive position in U.S. natural gas if the transaction closes.

Robust operating and free cash flow gives EQT internal funding capacity for debt reduction, infrastructure investment and shareholder returns. Although conversion varies across cycles, this cash-generation profile provides financial flexibility and supports resilience through weaker commodity-price environments.

Production outperformance, improved drilling and compression performance, and new contracted outlets can strengthen EQT’s volume reliability and commercial reach. Power and LNG arrangements also diversify demand exposure, potentially improving cash-flow visibility beyond spot Appalachian gas markets over time.

bear.b: EQT remains economically tied to natural-gas prices, so revenue and earnings can change sharply even when operating execution is strong. The recent TTM decline and prior loss years demonstrate that commodity cyclicality can weaken earnings durability, free-cash-flow conversion and returns.

bear.t: Low Gas Prices And Limited Hedging
bear.b: Weak realized gas prices directly pressure revenue and cash generation, while limited additional hedging leaves more future output exposed to market movements. Permian growth and weather-related downside risks could therefore amplify near-term volatility in operating cash flow and investment capacity.

EQT’s future demand and takeaway benefits depend on projects that are years from realization or still require approvals. Pulling capital forward increases near-term execution exposure, while delays to LNG, Southgate or the proposed Range merger could postpone expected scale, connectivity and cash-flow benefits.
